slides.title: AI Coaching for Accelerating Human Skill Development with Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: RL-BASED AI COACHING FOR MOTOR-SKILL DEVELOPMENT
slides.highlight: This work proposes a reinforcement learning framework for AI coaching that uses adaptive shared control to accelerate human motor-skill development, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on adaptive AI coaching to improve human proficiency.

card.one_liner: An RL-based AI coach that accelerates human motor-skill development by strategically modulating assistance to encourage productive failure.
card.key_idea: Formalizes coaching as a non-cooperative game using a probabilistic automaton to model skill evolution and a blending rule for adaptive shared control.
card.evaluation: User study (N=33) in FPV drone racing; L2C significantly reduced lap times (27.9%) and failures compared to RBF and MIA baselines.
card.limitation: Simulated learners may not capture the full variability of real human learning in more complex motor-skill settings.

slides.title: RoboScience Unveils Visics, a General-Purpose Embodied AI Model
slides.highlight: The introduction of Visics, a general-purpose embodied AI model, is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

slides.title: Decomposing Financial Market Dynamics via Mechanism Analysis in an Evolutionary Multi-Agent Simulation
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how specific mechanisms in an evolutionary multi-agent simulation control emergent properties like diversity, realism, and fragility, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: Financial market ABM mechanisms act as separable control knobs for diversity, realism, and fragility.
card.key_idea: A simulator with pluggable selection, microstructure, behavioral bias, and consensus topology mechanisms was tested via single-mechanism interventions to decompose their effects on emergent market properties.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using 3 scenarios, 20 seeds, and 50 generations. Metrics included strategy entropy, 5-fact realism, and fragility proxies; results used sign-tests and bootstrap CIs.
card.limitation: Uses proxies for fragility and cycling; realism excludes bubble-crash facts; results from a single simulator using synthetic/semi-historical scenarios.

slides.title: A Taxonomy of Conceptual Alignment in Human-Robot Dialogue
slides.tldr: TAXONOMY FOR CONCEPTUAL ALIGNMENT IN HRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a taxonomy and dialogue act schema to analyze and design how humans and robots co-construct conceptual alignment during interaction, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A design-centric taxonomy for analyzing and designing bidirectional conceptual alignment in human-robot dialogue.
card.key_idea: A framework characterizing alignment by initiation triggers (terminology, behaviors, situation), five levels of conceptual representation, and a detailed dialogue act schema for interactional moves.
card.evaluation: Instantiated via empirical analysis of 48 human-human dialogues in a collaborative image-sorting task to capture natural alignment behaviors.
card.limitation: Based on controlled tasks and human-only dialogues, potentially omitting in-the-wild dynamics and specific robotic constraints.

slides.title: When Robots Rate Their Own Interactions: Engagement Validity and the Strangeness Failure
slides.highlight: This research explores inverted evaluation where LLM-powered robots rate their own interactions, providing insights into the boundary conditions of using AI as interaction evaluators for RwB.

card.one_liner: LLM-powered robots can accurately rate interaction engagement but systematically fail to detect human strangeness/discomfort.
card.key_idea: An 'inverted evaluation' framework where LLMs complete standardized HRI questionnaires (HRI-CUES, Godspeed, RoSAS) from the robot's perspective using interaction transcripts and multimodal context.
card.evaluation: Tested via HRI-CUES dataset (1,522 evaluations across 5 LLMs) and a live Nao robot pilot (N=4). Results show moderate-to-strong engagement agreement but negative comfort correlations.
card.limitation: LLMs lack access to internal affective states, misinterpreting philosophical curiosity as comfort and requiring supplementary physiological or behavioral sensing modalities.

slides.title: AI-Mediated Negotiation: Design Reflections and Lessons
slides.highlight: This research evaluates a theory-driven AI coaching system, offering insights into how conversational AI can be designed to improve human strategic competence and reduce cognitive load, relevant to MOSAIC's adaptive AI coaching goals.

card.one_liner: Conversational AI coaching for negotiations can hinder empowerment by imposing linear structures on recursive tasks.
card.key_idea: Trucey used situational calibration, role-simulation, chunked delivery, and scaffolding, but found that linear conversational models mismatch the recursive cognitive demands of negotiation preparation.
card.evaluation: Pre-registered experiment (N=267) and interviews (N=15) comparing Trucey, a generic LLM, and a static handbook; handbook outperformed AI in empowerment and usability.
card.limitation: Qualitative sample was skewed toward early-career tech professionals; cognitive load and navigation effort were not measured directly.

slides.title: Real-Time Voice AI Hears but Does Not Listen
slides.tldr: EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE GAP IN VOICE AI
slides.highlight: This research identifies a disconnect between perception and action in real-time voice AI, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Real-time voice AIs prioritize spoken words over vocal delivery, ignoring critical emotional cues during decision-making.
card.key_idea: The 'emotional intelligence gap': systems perceive emotions (distress, sarcasm) in single-turn diagnostics but disregard them in multi-turn consequential scenarios, acting as if speech were a transcript.
card.evaluation: Four production systems (GPT Realtime 2, Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, Qwen3.5 Omni Plus/Flash) tested via multi-turn scenarios and single-turn diagnostics using synthesized audio.
card.limitation: Prompting systems to attend to delivery only partially and inconsistently improves performance, failing to fully close the gap.

slides.title: GROVE: Grounded Pedestrian Simulation via Natural Language for Interactive Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: GROVE enables the generation of realistic, socially challenging pedestrian scenarios via natural language, helping to narrow the sim2real gap for social robot navigation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: GROVE is a text-to-scenario framework generating realistic, grounded pedestrian simulations for social robot navigation training.
card.key_idea: Combines LLMs with RAG-based behavior tree generation, Theta* global planning, and Social Force Models to translate natural language prompts into executable, multi-horizon pedestrian behaviors.
card.evaluation: Compared against Text-Crowd and TRACE using VLM-based scoring (GPT-5) and trajectory visualization in hospital, office, and residential environments; GROVE showed superior prompt alignment.
card.limitation: High computational inference costs and a reliance on static obstacle maps, ignoring dynamic environmental changes like moving furniture.

slides.title: Students' Perception Accuracy of Partners' AI Use and its Relation to Collaboration Performance
slides.highlight: This study examines how misaligned perceptions of a partner's AI use affect team performance, relating to HyECHO's focus on modeling engagement and team state in hybrid human-AI settings.

card.one_liner: Misalignment in partners' perceptions of AI use correlates with lower final project scores in programming collaborations.
card.key_idea: A longitudinal study examining how accurately students perceive their partners' AI tool usage and how this perception gap impacts overall team performance.
card.evaluation: Three-wave longitudinal study of 103 student pairs in an introductory software engineering course; analyzed final project scores and prior performance.
card.limitation: Perception misalignment does not consistently decrease even with face-to-face pair-programming sessions.

slides.title: When Does Intrinsic Self-Correction Help? A Task-Sensitive Analysis
slides.highlight: This research examines how intrinsic self-correction serves as a task-dependent inference-time strategy, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: Intrinsic self-correction effectiveness depends on task structure, specifically verifiability and reasoning intensity, rather than being universally reliable.
card.key_idea: Analyzed self-correction across verifiable (SAT), reasoning-intensive (BBEH, HLE), and word-game tasks using two-step and three-step protocols across five diverse LLMs.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using accuracy and task-specific scores on six benchmarks; results show significant gains on highly verifiable tasks (e.g., SAT).
card.limitation: Does not cover open-ended generation (writing, coding) and relies on LLM-judges for sub-task reasoning and verifiability scoring.

slides.title: Predictive Gaze Is Preserved but Reorganized toward Monitoring during Robot-Mediated Manipulation
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that predictive gaze remains aligned with task goals during robot-mediated manipulation but shifts toward monitoring the end-effector, providing a signal for inferring intentions in human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: Predictive gaze is preserved during robot telemanipulation but shifts more toward monitoring the end-effector.
card.key_idea: Investigation of gaze behavior during goal-directed telemanipulation to determine how visuomotor control adapts to altered embodiment and disrupted sensorimotor coupling.

slides.title: A Dynamic Coupling Theory of Expertise Through Thinking Flow and Workflow Evolution
slides.highlight: This paper proposes Workflow Cognition to define expertise as a dynamic coupling of thinking flow and workflow evolution, providing a foundation for computational representations of human expertise in AI+Expert systems relevant to MOSAIC's focus on procedural and tacit skill.

card.one_liner: Proposes Workflow Cognition, a theory defining expertise as an emergent process rather than a static possession.
card.key_idea: Expertise emerges from the recursive dynamic coupling between 'Thinking Flow' (cognitive processes) and 'Workflow Evolution' (adaptation of actions and strategies) over longitudinal professional experience.
card.evaluation: The framework was explored through comparative qualitative analyses of illustrative expert cases in craftsmanship, creative production, education, and leadership.
card.limitation: The paper provides a theoretical foundation and illustrative examples rather than empirical validation or quantitative testing.

slides.title: SupplyNet: Supporting Visual Exploratory Learning in Supply Chain via Contextual Multi-Agent Simulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a contextual graph-based LLM multi-agent framework for supply chain simulation, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models and societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: SupplyNet is a gamified, LLM-powered visual simulation system for learning supply chain dynamics through exploration.
card.key_idea: A contextual multi-agent framework using LLMs for agent reasoning, paired with a graph view, branching 'what-if' timeline, and a task-oriented analysis console.
card.evaluation: A user study compared SupplyNet to a classic baseline simulation; participants reported increased engagement and improved perceived understanding of supply chain dynamics.

slides.title: SignVLA: Real-Time Sign Language-Guided Robotic Manipulation via Attention LSTM and Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: SignVLA introduces a framework for accessible human-robot interaction by converting sign language gestures into instructions for robotic manipulation, supporting the RwB goal of inclusive embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: SignVLA enables real-time robotic manipulation guided by sign language via a lightweight sign-to-text interface.
card.key_idea: MediaPipe hand landmarks are processed by an attention-enhanced LSTM and temporal buffer to generate natural-language instructions for a downstream GR00T VLA policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ASL Citizen (recognition) and LIBERO (manipulation). Attn-LSTM achieved 88.89% top-1 accuracy; GR00T reached up to 98.5% task success rate.
card.limitation: Real-world physical deployment and data collection on the Franka Emika robot remain as future work.

slides.title: Designing an OpenHarness Style Agent Runtime
slides.highlight: This exploration of agent runtimes featuring tools, memory, and multi-agent coordination is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

slides.title: Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning
slides.highlight: The EDV framework prevents cumulative errors in agent self-evolution by decoupling execution, distillation, and verification, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goals of self-monitoring and self-correction.

card.one_liner: EDV prevents agents from reinforcing errors by decoupling experience execution, distillation, and verification via multi-agent collaboration.
card.key_idea: A framework using heterogeneous agents for parallel execution, a third-party agent for contrastive distillation, and a consensus-based verification mechanism to filter noisy experience before memory insertion.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on τ²-bench, Mind2Web, and MMTB against baselines like ReasoningBank. Results show consistent performance gains and improved memory quality via human audit.

slides.title: STEB: A Speech-to-Speech Translation Expressiveness Benchmark for Evaluating Beyond Translation Fidelity
slides.highlight: This work introduces STEB to evaluate the preservation of emotion, scenario style, and nonverbal vocalizations in speech-to-speech translation, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: STEB is a Chinese-English benchmark evaluating S2ST expressiveness, including emotion, scenario style, and nonverbal vocalizations.
card.key_idea: A reference-free LLM-as-a-judge framework using a caption-then-summarize pipeline to compare structured expressive attributes between source and translated speech.
card.evaluation: Evaluated six S2ST systems using BLEU, COMET, and LLM-judged scores. Human correlation studies show statistically significant agreement with the summary-based scorer.
card.limitation: Currently limited to Chinese-English pairs and depends on the captioning model's ability to perceive paralinguistic cues.

slides.title: P-JEPA: Procedural Video Representation Learning via Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture
slides.highlight: P-JEPA enables long-form understanding of procedural steps in videos over 30 minutes, supporting the estimation of procedural skills and activity understanding relevant to MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: P-JEPA learns long-duration procedural video representations using masked latent prediction over dense frame-aligned features.
card.key_idea: A backbone-agnostic JEPA framework using clip-causal attention and 2D rotary positional embeddings to predict masked latent vectors in videos over 30 minutes long.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on EgoExo4D, EgoProceL, and Assembly101 using linear and temporal probes; achieved SOTA fine-grained action classification on EgoExo4D and improved temporal segmentation.
card.limitation: Clip-causal attention requires segment boundaries, which may not be available in real-world live video capture settings.

slides.title: Inverse Turing Bench: Evaluating Language Models as Judges of Human vs. AI Dialogue
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING AI ABILITY TO DIFFERENTIATE HUMANS FROM AI IN DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark to evaluate an AI's ability to distinguish between human-human and human-AI dialogues, serving as a probe for theory of mind relevant to ADAM-CHAT.

card.one_liner: Inverse Turing Bench evaluates the ability of LLMs and statistical tools to distinguish human-human from human-AI dialogues.
card.key_idea: A benchmark using paired multi-turn transcripts where judges must identify the human-only conversation, comparing token-probability-based detectors against zero-shot LLM-as-a-judge approaches.
card.evaluation: Tested various models (e.g., GPTZero, Claude Opus-4.6, GPT-5.5) on 557 dialogue pairs. GPTZero achieved the highest accuracy at 89.41%.
card.limitation: Susceptible to persona-prompting attacks and may not account for more recent model families or diverse AI personas.

slides.title: Knowledge discovery and collaboration meet agentic AI with Fluid Topics and Guru
slides.highlight: The integration of agentic AI for knowledge discovery and collaboration is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on AI teammates that adapt to team goals.

slides.title: When Certainty Is an Artifact: Keyword Lexicon Blindness and the (Mis)Measurement of Rhetorical Stance
slides.tldr: LLM-BASED SEMANTIC CLASSIFICATION OUTPERFORMS KEYWORD LEXICONS IN MEASURING RHETORICAL STANCE
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that keyword lexicons can misidentify rhetorical stance due to syntactic and polysemy blindness, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of accurate social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: Keyword lexicons can create spurious correlations between negative sentiment and certainty that LLMs reveal as measurement artifacts.
card.key_idea: Comparing keyword-based scoring with LLM zero-shot classification on 32,625 sentences to identify structural failure modes: syntactic, polysemy, and categorical blindness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 85 interviews from four public intellectuals using three independent lexicons and two LLMs (Doubao, GPT-5.4) via Pearson correlations.
card.limitation: The study focuses on a specific subset of public intellectuals' interview transcripts, which may not generalize to all discourse types.
